Subject: Short sprint: pricing options for 3-week eval — capacity vs token approach

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency and the KV caching profile. We have one remaining procurement question before we can sign the 3-week evaluation SOW: we'd like clarity on whether to buy a timeboxed reserved capacity (GPU-hours) for the sprint or to purchase token credits as a buffer.

High level constraints from our side:
- We expect heavy batch encoding on week 2 (roughly 10M tokens total over 48 hours).
- We want predictable spend so we can align the eval with our budget window.
- We may need short bursts of additional concurrency during day 10–12 for a load test.

Can you outline the unit economics and any surge pricing for both approaches (reserved capacity hourly vs token credits)? Also include any bridge credit options if we overrun before converting to a committed plan.

Thanks,
Elaine

Hi Elaine — great to hear the demo landed well. Quick overview below; I'll follow with a one-page rate sheet (attached) and loop in David (SE) for the workload sizing notes.

Option A — Reserved timebox (recommended if you want predictability)
- 3-week reserved window purchased as "Sprint Pool" (prebooked GPU-hours).
- Unit: GPU-hour at $35/hr (g5d-class equivalent) for reserved pool; includes 10% burst credit pool for short surges.
- Advantages: predictable invoice, capacity guaranteed, simple conversion path to Dedicated if you convert.

Option B — Token credits (recommended for token-dominated workloads)
- Prepaid token bundle calibrated to expected token use; standard token rate for the model is $0.0009/token for generation + $0.0002/token for embeddings (example).
- Advantages: pays only for tokens used; flexible but spend can spike during test-run anomalies.

Surge / bridge approach
- If you exceed reserved pool, we can provide a short-term burst rate of $55/hr for additional GPU-hours billed pro-rata.
- If you exceed tokens, we will bill overage at a 25% premium on the token rate or offer an emergency credit drawdown from a pre-funded buffer (recommended).

Conversion credit
- If you convert to a 12-month commit within 30 days after the eval, we'll apply up to 30% of unused reserved spend (or token spend up to $10k) as a conversion credit toward the first invoice.

I attached a suggested 3-week ratecard ("3-week-ratecard.xlsx") and a short SOW with milestones. Marcus/David — can you confirm the load test sizing and whether the 10% burst pool will cover the day-10 run?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — quick sizing note for Elaine: based on the description (10M tokens in ~48 hours), that maps to roughly 7–9 concurrent workers hitting the inference endpoints for ~48 hours. If you pick the reserved timebox, the 10% burst pool will likely be tight; I'd recommend either:

- Increasing the reserved pool by 15% to provide headroom, OR
- Keeping the reserved pool as-is and pre-provisioning a 6-hour surge block at the burst rate (billed only if used).

If they go token credits, ensure the token bundle includes a 20% safety margin and enable the pre-funded buffer so we can auto-top it to avoid request failures during load tests.

I'll drop a short Sizing note into the Drive link with expected GPU-hour numbers.

— David

Elaine — quick commercial tradeoffs to consider when you discuss this with procurement: 

- Predictability vs flexibility: Reserved pool gives a hard spend cap (you know the maximum), tokens lower the floor but can spike the ceiling.
- Procurement friendliness: Some procurement teams prefer a timebox SKU (line item for GPU-hours) because it's easy to tie to a purchase order; tokens sometimes require a prepaid credit note.
- Conversion mechanics: If you plan to convert to an annual committed contract, the reserved pool converts more cleanly into a Dedicated discount path.

Suggested final structure for your 3-week SOW (to speed PO):
1) Base: 3-week Sprint Pool: 1,200 GPU-hours at $35/hr = $42,000
2) Surge protection: 6 hours pre-provisioned at $55/hr = $330 (billed only if used)
3) Optional token topup: $10,000 pre-funded buffer for embedding-heavy tasks
4) Conversion credit: up to 30% of unused Sprint Pool applied to first year if commit executed in 30 days

If that looks reasonable I'll ask Legal to produce an addendum for your PO template.

Regards,
